rows.title: Primitive vocabulary package
rows.exact_statement: Define description, system, state, axis, continuum, boundary, operator, constraint, contradiction, resolution, collapse, and dimension birth with type signatures and falsifier checks.
rows.falsifier: A term has no type signature, source anchor, or failure check.
rows.acceptance_criteria: All primitive definitions have source refs, type signatures, counterexample/falsifier checks, and no circular dependence on the central principle.

rows.title: Central principle theorem/axiom/refutation decision
rows.exact_statement: An unresolved contradiction either gives rise to a new dimension of description or collapses the configuration that cannot resolve it.
rows.falsifier: A persistent unresolved contradiction exists that neither requires a new axis nor damages the relevant configuration, under the stated trigger conditions.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Decide PROVED_THEOREM, AXIOM_ACCEPTED_WITH_BOUNDARY, or REFUTED_AND_REPAIRED with proof/countermodel and article boundary.

rows.title: Operator catalog recovery
rows.exact_statement: The OC operator catalog consists of Birth, Differentiate, Stabilize, Project, Kill, and Repair as source-bound operator nodes.
rows.falsifier: A source-required operator is missing or a listed operator lacks a role/type signature.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Recover exact list, roles, type signatures, closure/composition obligations, and article boundary.

rows.title: Operator minimality and independence
rows.exact_statement: The source operator set is locally minimal for the chosen OC formalism.
rows.falsifier: One operator can be defined from the others without loss over the stated model class.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Provide one independence model per operator or repair the minimality claim.

rows.title: Operator closure and composition laws
rows.exact_statement: OC operators have well-defined closure and composition behavior over typed descriptions.
rows.falsifier: A claimed composition has no domain/codomain or violates preservation/loss conditions.
rows.acceptance_criteria: State closure/composition laws and prove them in the selected formalism.

rows.title: K0-K12 hierarchy definition package
rows.exact_statement: OC source K-levels K0 through K12 form a stated hierarchy from distinguishability to semantic super-continuum/global coherence.
rows.falsifier: A level lacks a definition, invariant, construction rule, or distinctness condition.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Recover definitions, construction rule, invariants, and article boundary for each level.

rows.title: Adjacent K-Level Non-Recovery Theorem
rows.exact_statement: Adjacent K-levels are non-collapsible under the 024 typed-extension formalism when the higher level carries a typed invariant not definable from the lower-level reduct.
rows.falsifier: Two levels are interdefinable without loss in the selected model class.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Prove distinctness or demote affected levels to conjectural extension.

rows.title: K-Level Count and Partition Repair
rows.exact_statement: The strong claim that K0-K12 is a unique, exhaustive, or minimal hierarchy is not proved; it is repaired to a source-bound ladder plus typed adjacent non-recovery.
rows.falsifier: A different partition covers the same phenomena with equal or better invariants and fewer assumptions.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Prove count/partition theorem or restrict article scope to a proved subhierarchy.

rows.title: OC Claim Admissibility Theorem
rows.exact_statement: Any article-eligible OC claim invoking the central schema must name description, system, active constraints, target organization predicate, admissible same-description repair/operator class, unresolvedness argument, and either necessary new axis or collapse certificate.
rows.falsifier: All consequences are definitional restatements or circular.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Produce a theorem with assumptions, proof, countermodel boundary, and independent verification.

rows.title: Law Candidate Classification Rule
rows.exact_statement: Every OC law-like statement must be classified as theorem consequence, axiom schema, empirical/domain conjecture, or excluded metaphor.
rows.falsifier: A law-like sentence has no status class or proof/evidence boundary.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Classify all law candidates before publication wording.

rows.title: Crown Stones Excluded From Core
rows.exact_statement: Crown-stone claims are conjectural extensions unless individually bound to a closed theorem chain.
rows.falsifier: A crown-stone claim is promoted while its dependency path is open.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Map each crown-stone claim to proof chain or mark conjectural/excluded.

rows.title: Domain Projections Excluded From Core
rows.exact_statement: Domain projections are applications requiring local variables, constraints, operators, organization predicates, evidence, and falsifiers; they are not core validation.
rows.falsifier: A projection is treated as global validation without local evidence and falsifier.
rows.acceptance_criteria: Bind each projection to local evidence or exclude from core article.

rows.title: Bounded Article Eligibility Theorem
rows.exact_statement: The closed 024 core is article-eligible only as a bounded axiomatic theory with explicit conjectural exclusions and no universal-law wording.
rows.falsifier: The article draft uses stronger wording than the proof ledger permits.
rows.acceptance_criteria: No promoted wording exceeds DB proof status and boundary file.
